consensus_summary: Primary consensus identifies 'heart of the earth' as Jesus's burial in the grave/tomb (or extended to Hades/Sheol, the realm of the dead) for the three days and nights of Matthew 12:40, typologically parallel to Jonah in the fish.
book_summary: Jerusalem as the navel and heart of the land.
consensus_core_identification: Christ's grave/tomb or Hades (realm of the dead)
boundary_disagreement: Book replaces the consensus primary referent (grave/Hades) with Jerusalem, which consensus lists only as a minority/rare alternative mainly for chronological reasons; no shared central category is preserved.
material_contradiction: The same phrase cannot simultaneously have the grave/Hades and Jerusalem as its core referent in the same sense; accepting the book requires rejecting the consensus primary identification of Matthew 12:40.
rationale: All three consensus responses converge on grave/tomb or Hades as the settled primary meaning drawn from the Jonah typology of Matt 12:40 (with common extensions to descent). The book instead asserts Jerusalem via the 'midst/navel' language of Ezek 5:5/38:12, a view the consensus itself flags only as minority/rare. Cores are incompatible referents, not a narrowing/broadening of the same category.
strongest_objection: The explicit Jonah parallel in Matt 12:40 (three days/nights in the fish's belly = heart of the earth) forces a death/burial/confinement reading far more directly than a geographic identification of Jerusalem as the earth's center.
